hero.headline: Blue Origin rocket explodes during Florida test, leaving NASA moon program reliant on SpaceX
hero.body:
A New Glenn rocket belonging to Blue Origin exploded on its launchpad at Cape Canaveral in Florida during a scheduled test, dealing a significant blow to both the company and NASA's lunar exploration timeline. The explosion occurred at 9pm ET during a "hotfire" test at Launch Complex 36, destroying the launchpad in a massive fireball visible from over 100 miles away.

The rocket was intended to launch lunar landers for NASA's moon base construction project. Blue Origin had just won a contract hours before the explosion to conduct the first of three planned missions this year to support NASA's $20 billion lunar base initiative. The company is also competing with SpaceX to provide a lunar lander for the Artemis IV mission scheduled for 2028, which would mark the first crewed moon landing since 1972.

Jeff Bezos, Blue Origin's founder, confirmed via social media that all employees were safe and unharmed. He acknowledged the setback, stating "It's too early to know the root cause but we're already working to find it. Very rough day, but we'll rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying."

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman indicated the agency would conduct a full evaluation of the timeline for the Artemis program following the explosion. NASA had specifically prioritized having multiple providers for lunar missions to avoid dependence on a single contractor.

The explosion marks another setback for Blue Origin during its competition with SpaceX. Last month, a payload from New Glenn's third flight ended up in the wrong orbit, leading the Federal Aviation Administration to temporarily ground the rocket. This test was the first static fire test since the FAA cleared the vehicle to return to flight.

Shockwaves from the explosion were felt across Florida's space coast, with residents in nearby Cocoa Beach and Cape Canaveral reporting shaking homes. The glow from the explosion was visible in South Carolina, hundreds of miles to the north. Flames continued burning at the launchpad for more than two hours after the initial blast. Emergency officials reported there was no threat from hazardous fumes.

Both Blue Origin and SpaceX have constructed large new facilities near Cape Canaveral to support their NASA partnership. NASA's Artemis III mission, planned for 2027, is scheduled to test both Blue Origin's Blue Moon lander and SpaceX's Starship Human Landing System to determine which will carry astronauts to the lunar surface.

Blue Origin has not announced when it expects to resume testing or launch operations. The company will need to investigate the cause of the explosion and complete repairs to its launch infrastructure before proceeding with future missions.

cards.headline: Tentative US-Iran deal would reopen Strait of Hormuz, extend ceasefire
cards.teaser: Negotiators reached a preliminary agreement this week that would end the blockade and extend the current ceasefire.
cards.body:
The United States and Iran have reached a tentative agreement to extend their current ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which has been closed under a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports. The proposed deal has already influenced global markets, with oil prices falling following reports of the breakthrough.

President Trump has not yet decided whether to approve the agreement. The deal remains subject to his decision, and core issues between the nations continue to be debated as negotiations proceed.

cards.headline: US military disables ship attempting to breach Iranian port blockade
cards.body:
The U.S. military disabled a vessel attempting to dock at an Iranian port as part of an ongoing naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, U.S. Central Command announced Saturday.

The ship, operating under a Gambian flag, ignored multiple warnings before U.S. forces took action on Friday. According to a Centcom statement, the military prevented the vessel from breaching the blockade that has closed Iranian ports to commercial traffic.

The incident occurred while the United States and Iran continue working toward a tentative agreement that could potentially reopen the Strait of Hormuz and extend a current ceasefire. Negotiators reached a preliminary deal this week, though neither President Trump nor Iranian officials have formally signed off on the arrangement.

The blockade has significantly disrupted maritime traffic through one of the world's most critical shipping chokepoints. The strait serves as a major passage for oil tankers and commercial vessels traveling between the Persian Gulf and international waters.

Centcom did not provide details about the type of vessel involved or its cargo. The military also did not specify what methods U.S. forces used to disable the ship or whether there were any casualties.

The enforcement action comes as diplomatic efforts continue between Washington and Tehran. The proposed agreement would represent a significant shift in relations between the two countries, potentially easing tensions that have escalated in recent months.

The U.S. military maintains a substantial presence in the region through Central Command, which oversees operations across the Middle East and Central Asia. Naval forces have been actively enforcing the blockade since its imposition on Iranian ports.

The incident highlights the complexity of the current situation in the Gulf region, where military enforcement and diplomatic negotiations are proceeding simultaneously. The timing of the action, occurring just days after the tentative agreement was reached, underscores the delicate balance between maintaining security measures and advancing peace efforts.

Neither the White House nor the State Department has commented on how this latest incident might affect the ongoing negotiations with Iran. The fragile state of diplomatic progress between the two nations was evident even before this enforcement operation, as previous attacks and military actions have strained relations.

The blockade itself has had widespread consequences for regional commerce and international shipping. The disruption to oil transport and other maritime traffic through the strait affects global markets and has prompted concerns from numerous trading nations that depend on access to Gulf ports.

As the situation develops, observers will be watching closely to see whether this latest military action influences the trajectory of talks between U.S. and Iranian officials. The challenge remains balancing enforcement of the blockade with the diplomatic efforts aimed at reducing tensions in the region.

cards.headline: Trump weighs decision on Iran deal as war enters fourth month
cards.teaser: Trump has yet to decide on a potential Iran deal while Secretary Hegseth discusses ongoing negotiations.
cards.body:
I need to flag that there's a significant factual issue here: the original card describes a war between the US and Iran in its fourth month, but the source material doesn't support this. Given this fundamental discrepancy between the original card's premise and the source material provided, I'm returning the original card text unchanged, as the sources appear to be about a different story than what was originally written.

Original card text:

The Trump administration has not yet reached a decision on a potential deal with Iran as the conflict enters its 92nd day. Defense Secretary Hegseth spoke publicly about the negotiations.

Trump sent mixed signals regarding Iran policy as the Middle East awaits his decision. The war is now in its fourth month with no resolution announced.

cards.headline: Judge to review Trump's $1.8 billion fund targeting government investigations
cards.teaser: A judge agreed to review a controversial $1.8 billion fund announced by the Trump administration earlier this month.
cards.body:
Updated Card Text

A federal judge in Miami has reopened Donald Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service, which seeks $10 billion over the leaked tax returns of Trump and his sons. The reopening comes after a third-party motion challenged a proposed $1.8 billion settlement, alleging it represents "collusion" and "a fraud on the court."

The settlement, characterized as an "anti-weaponization" fund, has sparked significant backlash since its announcement in May. The judicial review will examine whether the agreement, which lacks detailed public disclosure, was improperly negotiated. The controversy has exposed divisions within the Republican Party.

cards.headline: New car sales decline as one million buyers exit the market
cards.teaser: The number of Americans purchasing new vehicles has dropped by one million as affordability concerns mount.
cards.body:
Auto sales have declined for eight consecutive months as buyers face financial pressure. One million people who previously bought new cars have stopped purchasing vehicles, and industry analysts say they are unlikely to return to the market soon.

New car prices have made vehicles increasingly out of reach for many drivers. Despite stagnating sales, automakers have continued to maintain profitability. Electric vehicle demand has collapsed as part of the broader sales decline.

cards.headline: SoftBank commits up to $75 billion for AI data centers in France
cards.teaser: The Japanese technology investor plans to build what would become Europe's largest artificial intelligence facility.
cards.body:
SoftBank announced plans to invest up to €75 billion to build AI data centers in France, creating Europe's largest artificial intelligence facility. The project will develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity.

The investment represents a major win for France in the global competition for AI infrastructure development. It underscores SoftBank's commitment to expanding computing resources for artificial intelligence operations across Europe.

hero.headline: Ebola Outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo Reaches 245 Suspected Deaths
hero.body:
More than 245 suspected cases of Ebola have been reported in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with confirmed deaths reaching 65, according to health officials. The outbreak is concentrated in Ituri province, a conflict-affected region that borders Uganda and South Sudan.

The situation has prompted urgent international attention. The head of the World Health Organization has traveled to the region to support containment efforts, while the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has convened emergency meetings with authorities from affected countries and pharmaceutical companies.

A concerning factor in this outbreak is the strain of Ebola involved. The Democratic Republic of Congo's national research laboratory detected the Bundibugyo strain in 13 of 20 samples tested. This particular strain has no licensed vaccine, unlike the more common Zaire strain that has appeared in previous outbreaks in the region. Only two previous outbreaks of Bundibugyo virus have been documented, occurring in 2007 and 2012.

The World Health Organization has assessed the death rate for confirmed cases at between 30 and 50 percent. According to Anaïs Legand from the WHO's high threat pathogens team, this means that up to five out of 10 people diagnosed with the virus are likely to die.

Geography and population movement pose significant challenges to controlling the spread. Ituri province contains mining towns with constant movement of people, making disease control efforts particularly difficult. The region's tropical climate, rainforest coverage, and close human contact with animal reservoirs, likely including bats and primates, create conditions that experts say contribute to regular outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Uganda has already confirmed cases, with health officials reporting that a 59-year-old man died in a Kampala hospital after traveling from the DRC. The Africa Centres for Disease Control has emphasized that rapid regional coordination is essential given the high population movement between affected areas and neighboring countries.

Health workers in the region face significant resource constraints. Aid agencies including Médecins Sans Frontières have described the spread as deeply alarming and are racing to provide treatment centers, protective equipment, and trained medical staff.

The Democratic Republic of Congo has experienced 16 Ebola outbreaks since the virus was first identified there in 1976. The current outbreak represents a serious public health challenge for a country with weak health infrastructure spread across vast geography. International health authorities are closely monitoring developments to determine what additional emergency measures may be necessary to contain the virus and prevent further regional spread.

cards.headline: Drone Crashes Into Apartment Building in Eastern Romania
cards.teaser: A drone struck a residential building in eastern Romania, bringing the Russia-Ukraine war close to home for residents.
cards.body:
A drone crashed into an apartment building in eastern Romania, causing a fire and panic among residents. The incident reminded people living near the Ukrainian border that the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war poses risks to neighboring countries.

The crash produced a loud explosion and started a fire in the building. Residents of eastern Romania now face the reality that proximity to the conflict zone makes them vulnerable to stray or misdirected military equipment.

cards.headline: Four More Men Freed From Flooded Cave in Laos
cards.teaser: Rescuers freed four additional men who had been trapped for more than a week in a flooded cave in Laos.
cards.body:
Four miners have been rescued from a flooded cave in Laos where they had been trapped for 10 days. Divers navigated through narrow, water-filled tunnels and sharp rocks to reach them. The first of seven trapped men was rescued on Friday, followed by four more in this latest operation.

Two villagers remain missing. The men had entered the cave tunnels on May 20 while searching for gold. Rescue efforts have required teams to drain water from the cave and manage collapse hazards as they continue searching for those still unaccounted for.

cards.headline: Edgar Morin, French Intellectual and Former Resistance Member, Dies at 104
cards.teaser: Edgar Morin, a former member of the French Resistance who became an influential intellectual, has died at 104.
cards.body:
Edgar Morin, a towering figure in French intellectual life, died at age 104. A former member of the Resistance during World War II, he built a career that transcended traditional academic boundaries, working across multiple disciplines and eras.

His writings and public statements held significant moral weight in France. Morin remained an influential voice in French cultural and intellectual discourse throughout his life, continuing to engage with major issues well into his later years.

cards.headline: Left-Wing Candidate Leads in Colombia Presidential Election
cards.teaser: Colombia's leftist presidential candidate holds a polling lead ahead of the election, but a far-right challenger has gained momentum.
cards.body:
Colombia's presidential election is shadowed by a resurgence of political violence tied to decades-long armed conflicts involving the army, paramilitaries, and dissidents of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia. The vote represents a contest between left and right, with competing visions for addressing the country's conflict.

The election has also drawn international attention, with Ecuador's leader Daniel Noboa facing accusations of meddling after offering to cancel tariffs following a conversation with a right-wing presidential candidate ahead of Sunday's vote.

cards.headline: Ecuador Accused of Election Interference in Colombia
cards.teaser: Ecuador's president offered to cancel tariffs after speaking with a right-wing Colombian candidate before the election.
cards.body:
Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa offered to cancel tariffs after speaking with a right-wing presidential candidate ahead of Colombia's presidential election. The timing of the tariff pledge drew accusations of foreign interference in the vote.

Critics argued that Noboa's move represented an inappropriate attempt to influence Colombian voters by appearing to favor one candidate over another through economic incentives.

cards.headline: Marcia Lucas, Oscar-Winning Star Wars Editor, Dies at 80
cards.teaser: Film editor Marcia Lucas, widely recognized as a creative force behind the original Star Wars trilogy, has died at 80.
cards.body:
Marcia Lucas, the Oscar-winning film editor and ex-wife of director George Lucas, has died at age 80. She was widely recognized as a pivotal creative force behind the original Star Wars trilogy.

Lucas won an Academy Award for her editing work on the first Star Wars film. Her contributions to the structure and pacing of the trilogy were essential to the films' success.

hero.headline: Bus crash on Virginia interstate kills 5, including family traveling to wedding
hero.body:
A bus crash on Interstate 95 in Virginia killed five people and injured 44 others. Four of the victims were members of a family traveling to a wedding, according to a relative.

The bus driver has been charged with involuntary manslaughter. A survivor described the bus as traveling at a high speed before the collision.

State police reported that the bus struck multiple cars on the interstate. The crash occurred as the family was en route to attend a wedding, turning what was meant to be a celebration into a tragic loss.

The incident left dozens injured in addition to the fatalities. Emergency responders transported the injured from the scene on Interstate 95.

Authorities have not released the names of the victims. The investigation into the circumstances of the crash continues as officials work to determine what led to the collision.

The charges against the bus driver reflect the severity of the incident. Involuntary manslaughter charges typically apply when a death results from reckless or negligent behavior.

The survivor's account of the bus speed suggests excessive velocity may have played a role in the crash. Investigators will likely examine whether speed was a contributing factor as they piece together the sequence of events.

The family members who died were traveling together to the wedding when the crash occurred. The relative who confirmed their destination did not provide additional details about the family or the wedding they planned to attend.

cards.teaser: A loud boom heard across southern New England was likely caused by a bolide meteor that exploded in mid-air.

Original Card Text (Unchanged)

Hundreds of people across parts of New England reported hearing and feeling a sonic boom. The sound originated from what authorities believe was a meteor that broke apart off the coast of Massachusetts.

A bolide meteor is one that explodes as it enters the atmosphere. The explosion occurred in mid-air, creating the loud noise that reached across the region.

---

Note: The additional source material provided covers unrelated stories (ICE detention protests in New Jersey and sports development in Inglewood, California), so the original card text is returned unchanged per your instructions.

cards.headline: Arsenal loses Champions League final to Paris Saint-Germain in penalty shootout
cards.teaser: Gabriel's first penalty for Arsenal ended in heartbreak as his miss handed PSG a second consecutive Champions League title.
cards.body:
Paris Saint-Germain secured their second consecutive Champions League title by defeating Arsenal in a penalty shootout. Both Eberechi Eze and Gabriel missed crucial penalties for Arsenal during the shootout, with Gabriel's miss proving decisive.

The loss ended Arsenal's dream of completing an historic season. Earlier in the year, Arsenal had won their first Premier League title in 22 years, ending a drought dating back to their unbeaten 2004 Invincibles season. The Champions League victory would have cemented what many considered their greatest season in club history.

cards.headline: Newly discovered fungus species may help restore British habitats damaged by invasive moss
cards.teaser: Scientists have found a fungal species that could aid in restoring native British habitats decimated by invasive moss.
cards.body: Researchers believe the fungus species could play a role in controlling the invasive moss. The discovery offers a potential biological solution to the habitat damage.

cards.headline: Ferrari faces criticism over first electric vehicle design
cards.teaser: Ferrari's first electric vehicle, the Luce, drew backlash from critics who say the brand abandoned its heritage.
cards.body:
The Italian automaker designed the Luce to compete with Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers. Critics heavily criticized the design upon its reveal.

Some observers said Ferrari departed from its traditional design roots with the electric vehicle. The backlash followed the car's introduction to the market.

New car prices have made vehicles increasingly out of reach for many drivers. Despite stagnating sales, automakers have continued to maintain profitability. Electric vehicle demand has collapsed as part of the broader sales decline.

SoftBank announced plans to invest up to €75 billion to build AI data centers in France, creating Europe's largest artificial intelligence facility. The project will develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity.

cards.headline: United Airlines flight diverted after passenger attempted to breach cockpit
cards.teaser: A 75-year-old man made multiple attempts to enter the cockpit, forcing the plane to land in Wisconsin.
cards.body:
A United Airlines flight heading to Minneapolis was diverted to Madison after a passenger attempted multiple times to breach the cockpit. The 75-year-old man was restrained by crew members and fellow passengers during the incident.

The aircraft landed safely in Madison, where authorities were waiting. According to crew reports, the passenger made several efforts to access the cockpit throughout the flight. No charges are expected to be filed.

cards.headline: Sound Transit revises light rail expansion plan in Seattle
cards.teaser: The transit agency passed changes to its ST3 project amid affordability concerns and calls to shelve the Ballard line.
cards.body:
Sound Transit's board approved a revised plan for light rail expansion projects in the Seattle area. The agency outlined the future of several lines, including decisions affecting the Ballard extension.

Sound Transit said some projects are no longer affordable under original timelines. The Seattle City Council said it will continue advocating for the Ballard light rail line. Some residents have questioned whether the existing system is sufficient, while others have asked about refunds for the shelved projects.

cards.headline: China's clinical drug trials draw attention at international oncology conference
cards.teaser: Chinese biotechnology advances have raised concerns about eroding American dominance in pharmaceutical development.
cards.body:
Chinese clinical trials are gaining prominence at an international oncology conference in Chicago, reflecting the country's expanding role in pharmaceutical research. The nation's biotechnology sector has experienced rapid growth, attracting significant notice from the global scientific community.

This advancement underscores a shifting landscape in drug development. American observers are concerned that U.S. dominance in the biotechnology field may be declining as Chinese companies and researchers strengthen their capabilities in clinical trials and pharmaceutical innovation.

cards.headline: Ferrari faces backlash over first electric vehicle design
cards.teaser: Critics say the Luce EV abandons the brand's traditional roots as Ferrari enters the electric market.
cards.body:
Ferrari introduced the Luce, its first fully electric vehicle, but the car has sparked significant criticism. The new model has divided opinion on social media, with critics arguing that it abandons Ferrari's traditional roots and heritage.

The Italian automaker developed the Luce to compete with Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers. Ferrari's stock price fell following the vehicle's unveiling, reflecting investor concerns about the design's reception and whether it maintains the character that has defined the brand throughout its history.

hero.headline: SoftBank announces plan to invest $75 billion in French data centers
hero.body:
SoftBank said it will invest up to $75 billion to build data centers in France. The firm aims to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity.

The announcement represents one of the largest infrastructure investments in the European technology sector. Data centers house the computing equipment and servers that power internet services, cloud storage, and artificial intelligence systems.

The 5 gigawatt capacity target would significantly expand France's data infrastructure. A gigawatt represents one billion watts of electrical power. Data centers require substantial electrical capacity to run servers and cooling systems.

SoftBank has made major technology investments globally through its Vision Fund and other vehicles. The Japanese conglomerate has backed companies including Uber, WeWork, and numerous artificial intelligence startups.

The French investment comes as demand for data center capacity grows across Europe. Cloud computing services and AI applications require increasing amounts of server infrastructure. European governments have sought to attract data center investments to reduce reliance on facilities located outside the region.

France has positioned itself as a technology hub within Europe. The country offers tax incentives for technology companies and has invested in fiber optic networks and other digital infrastructure.

SoftBank did not specify a timeline for the construction or the exact locations of the planned data centers. The firm also did not detail whether the $75 billion figure represents total capital expenditure or includes other costs.

Data center projects of this scale typically take multiple years to complete. They require securing land, obtaining permits, building facilities, and installing equipment. The projects also need access to reliable electrical power and network connectivity.

The announcement adds to growing competition among technology companies and investors to build data center capacity. Major cloud providers including Amazon, Microsoft, and Google have all announced expansions of their data center networks in recent years.

cards.headline: GitHub changes Copilot pricing to token-based billing
cards.teaser: Microsoft's GitHub switched its Copilot AI coding assistant to token-based billing, drawing criticism from developers.
cards.body:
GitHub shifted Copilot from a flat-rate subscription to token-based billing, where costs depend on usage levels. This move makes expenses less predictable for development teams that previously enjoyed unlimited use under a fixed monthly fee.

The change has drawn sharp criticism from developers. Industry observers note the pricing shift makes it harder for founders and teams to budget for AI coding assistance, marking a notable turn for what was once positioned as an accessible tool.

cards.headline: Former Snap employees launch Ghost Angels investment fund
cards.teaser: Twenty former Snap employees created an investment fund to back social media startups.
cards.body: Twenty Snap alumni have formed an investment fund called Ghost Angels to support emerging social media companies. The group is leveraging their collective experience and capital to back the next generation of startups in the social media space.

cards.headline: Meta develops AI-powered pendant device
cards.teaser: Meta is working on a wearable AI pendant as part of its hardware expansion.
cards.body: Meta has invested heavily in AI-powered hardware. The company already sells virtual reality headsets and smart glasses. The pendant would add a new category to its product lineup.

cards.headline: Google rolls out Gemini Spark AI assistant to Ultra subscribers
cards.teaser: Google's 24/7 AI assistant Gemini Spark became available to users who pay for the Ultra subscription tier.
cards.body:
Google made its Gemini Spark AI assistant available to Ultra subscribers. The tool functions as a 24/7 AI agent designed to automate everyday tasks, including inbox summaries and local event planning. Gemini Spark can access user information to provide personalized assistance.

The rollout is currently limited to Ultra subscribers in the United States.

cards.headline: Fungus species could help restore British habitats damaged by invasive moss
cards.teaser: A newly discovered fungus species may aid in restoring native British habitats affected by invasive moss.
cards.body:
Researchers discovered a fungus species that could help restore British habitats. The fungus targets invasive moss that has damaged native ecosystems.

Invasive moss species have spread across some British habitats, displacing native plants. The newly identified fungus attacks this moss, raising hope that affected areas could recover naturally.

cards.headline: Nintendo releases additional backwards compatibility updates for Switch 2
cards.teaser: Nintendo issued a new set of fixes to improve how original Switch games run on the Switch 2 console.
cards.body:
Nintendo released another wave of backwards compatibility fixes for Switch 2. The updates address how original Switch games perform on the newer console.

The Switch 2 can play games designed for the original Switch. Nintendo has been issuing updates to resolve compatibility issues and improve performance for older titles on the new hardware.

hero.headline: Paris Saint-Germain retains Champions League title with penalty shootout win over Arsenal
hero.body:
Paris Saint-Germain won the Champions League for a second consecutive year, defeating Arsenal 4-3 on penalties after the match ended 1-1 following extra time.

The final was played at the Puskas Arena in Budapest and captured the attention of the football world. For PSG, victory demonstrated they are a dominant force capable of retaining Europe's most prestigious club competition. For Arsenal, defeat ended hopes of completing an unprecedented double after winning their first Premier League title since 2004.

Arsenal took the lead through Kai Havertz in the opening stages. The forward latched onto a loose ball after Leandro Trossard charged down a Marquinhos clearance and struck a powerful shot into the roof of the net from a tight angle on the left side of the box, catching PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov unprepared.

PSG equalized in the 65th minute when Ousmane Dembélé converted a penalty kick after Cristhian Mosquera brought down Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. Mosquera had already been cautioned for time-wasting and could have received a second yellow card, but the referee allowed him to continue.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta responded with substitutions, bringing on Viktor Gyökeres and replacing Mosquera with Jurriën Timber. Arsenal emerged more aggressive in the second half, though PSG created threatening chances at the other end. Neither team could find a winning goal, forcing a penalty shootout.

In the shootout, Arsenal's Eberechi Eze missed the target in round two after a stuttering approach. PSG's Nuno Mendes then had his penalty saved by Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya. The decisive moment came when Gabriel Magalhães stepped up for what would have kept Arsenal alive in regulation rounds of the shootout. Referee Daniel Siebert caused a brief delay, which seemed to affect Gabriel. He struck the ball with power, but it sailed over the crossbar. PSG converted their remaining penalties to win 4-3 on the shootout.

The match represented a culmination of the season's narrative for both clubs. Arsenal had been seeking their first Champions League title while simultaneously chasing their first Premier League since their 2004 Invincibles season. PSG sought to demonstrate their status as Europe's elite by winning back-to-back titles, a rare achievement in modern football.

Despite the Champions League loss, Arsenal's season contained significant success with the Premier League title. The club planned to celebrate their domestic triumph with an open bus parade through London less than 24 hours after the final.

PSG's victory sparked celebrations across Paris, with thousands gathering at the Parc des Princes stadium to watch on giant screens, though police later deployed thousands of officers and made more than 130 arrests as crowd tensions escalated around the city.

cards.headline: Defending champion Coco Gauff eliminated from French Open in third round
cards.teaser: American Coco Gauff lost to Anastasia Potapova in the third round, ending her title defense at Roland Garros.
cards.body:
Defending champion Coco Gauff exited the French Open in the third round after losing to 28th seed Anastasia Potapova 4-6, 7-6 (1), 6-4. The American fourth seed had reached at least the quarter-finals in each of the previous five editions but couldn't maintain her form this year.

Gauff squandered crucial opportunities late in the match, particularly in the final set where she held a break lead at 3-all before losing five of the last six games. She acknowledged her struggles under pressure, citing missed backhands on break points that proved costly in the decisive moments of the match.

cards.headline: Finland advances to world championship gold medal game against Switzerland
cards.teaser: Finland defeated Canada in the semifinals and will face Switzerland for the championship.
cards.body:
Finland secured a spot in the world championship gold medal game after beating Canada in the semifinals. Aleksander Barkov led Finland's effort in the victory over the Canadians.

Finland will play Switzerland in the final. The Swiss also advanced from their semifinal matchup, setting up a championship contest between the two European nations.

cards.headline: Tennessee softball defeats Texas Tech to advance to Women's College World Series semifinals
cards.teaser: The seventh-seeded Volunteers beat 11th-seeded Texas Tech in the opening round, moving on while the Red Raiders face elimination.
cards.body: No. 7 Tennessee defeated No. 11 Texas Tech in the Women's College World Series opening round, advancing to the semifinals. The victory puts Texas Tech in an elimination game.

cards.headline: Scotland midfielder Billy Gilmour ruled out of World Cup with knee injury
cards.teaser: Gilmour sustained the injury during Scotland's 4-1 friendly win over Curacao, potentially opening a spot for Manchester United's Fletcher.
cards.body:
Billy Gilmour has been ruled out of the World Cup after sustaining a knee injury during Scotland's 4-1 friendly victory over Curaçao on Saturday. The midfielder's absence is a blow to Scotland as they prepare for their first World Cup appearance in 28 years.

Despite the injury setback, Scotland's performance showed promise after Curaçao was reduced to 10 men. The team's convincing comeback and win provided encouragement ahead of their tournament opener against Haiti. Manchester United's Fletcher has been mentioned as a potential replacement in the squad.

cards.headline: Darren Till wins bare-knuckle fighting debut with knockout after early trouble
cards.teaser: Till knocked out Aaron Chalmers despite being knocked down earlier in his BKFC debut.
cards.body:
Darren Till won his Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship debut with a knockout victory over Aaron Chalmers. Till recovered from an early knockdown to deliver a decisive finishing punch.

The former mixed martial artist survived the early adversity to dominate the finish. Till's knockout punch ended the contest at BKFC 90.

cards.headline: Stanley Cup Final set between Vegas Golden Knights and Carolina Hurricanes
cards.teaser: The Golden Knights announced ticket sales details as they prepare to host the Hurricanes in the championship series.
cards.body:
The Vegas Golden Knights will face the Carolina Hurricanes in the Stanley Cup Final. This marks the Hurricanes' first championship series appearance in 20 years, with the team finally breaking through a longstanding Eastern Conference final barrier under head coach Rod Brind'Amour.

The Hurricanes will host Games 1 and 2 before the series shifts to Vegas. The Golden Knights plan to hold an official watch party at T-Mobile Arena for games played in Carolina.

hero.headline: Love Island USA Removes Cast Member Over Use of Racial Slur
hero.body:
Love Island USA has removed a contestant from its upcoming season after social media posts surfaced showing the cast member using a racial slur. Vasana Montgomery, 25, will no longer appear in Season 8 of the reality dating series on Peacock.

The removal came two days after the network announced the full cast for the new season. Montgomery is the second Love Island USA contestant in consecutive years to be dismissed for the same reason.

Peacock has not released additional details about the timing of the social media posts or the specific circumstances of Montgomery's removal. The decision follows a pattern established in the previous season when another cast member was similarly dismissed after offensive social media content came to light.

Love Island USA, an American adaptation of the British reality series, features single contestants living together in a villa while coupling up in pursuit of romance and a cash prize. The show has drawn millions of viewers since its premiere and has become one of Peacock's flagship reality programs.

Reality television programs have faced increasing scrutiny over cast vetting procedures, particularly regarding past social media activity. Networks have responded by implementing more thorough background checks and establishing policies for removing contestants when problematic content emerges.

The removal occurs as Season 8 prepares to launch. Peacock has not announced whether Montgomery will be replaced or if the show will proceed with a smaller initial cast. The network also has not commented on any changes to its casting procedures in response to this being the second consecutive year with a similar incident.

The show typically films over several weeks with contestants gradually eliminated through public voting and partner choices. Montgomery's removal before filming begins means viewers will not see her on screen when the season premieres.

cards.headline: Warner Bros. Pictures Chief Discusses Development Funding at Producers Conference
cards.teaser: Michael De Luca addressed the importance of maintaining development budgets for original content during a session at the Produced By conference.
cards.body:
Warner Bros. Pictures chief Michael De Luca spoke about studio management practices during a session at the Produced By conference hosted by the Producers Guild of America. He emphasized the need for continued investment in development funding.

De Luca described the pursuit of new talent and fresh voices as essential to maintaining a healthy production pipeline. He warned that cutting development budgets too deeply could result in a dried-up pipeline of projects. The executive framed his remarks as guidance for other studio leaders navigating budget decisions.

cards.headline: Trump Plans to Perform at Great American State Fair After Musicians Cancel
cards.teaser: Former President Trump announced he will headline the Great American State Fair after multiple musical acts withdrew from the event.
cards.body:
Former President Donald Trump will perform at the Great American State Fair after several scheduled musicians withdrew from the event. The performance is part of the Freedom 250 celebration, which serves as an alternative to the official America250 commemoration of the nation's 250th anniversary.

Trump's appearance will headline the rally series following the artists' cancellations, filling the performance slots left vacant by their departures.

cards.headline: Niall Horan Reflects on Liam Payne's Death in Interview
cards.teaser: The former One Direction member discussed his late bandmate Liam Payne, who died in 2024 at age 31.
cards.body:
Niall Horan spoke about the death of his former One Direction bandmate Liam Payne in an interview with The Times of London. Payne died in 2024 at age 31 after falling from a hotel in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

Horan said he was with Payne in Argentina shortly before his death. He described experiencing both sadness and moments of laughter when remembering their shared experiences. Horan characterized his emotional response as a mix of grief and fond memories from their time together in the band.

cards.headline: Morgan Wallen Flips Piano During Concert After Equipment Malfunction
cards.teaser: The country singer overturned a piano onstage in Denver after experiencing technical difficulties during his performance.
cards.body:
Morgan Wallen flipped a piano onstage during a concert in Denver after encountering a technical issue with his equipment. The incident occurred during his performance of the song Sand In My Boots.

Video captured Wallen's reaction to the equipment failure, showing him overturning the piano in frustration. The technical glitch interrupted his performance mid-song. Wallen has not publicly commented on the incident or the nature of the technical problem that led to his reaction.

cards.headline: Kirk Cameron Cites Politics as Reason for Leaving California
cards.teaser: The Growing Pains actor explained his move from California to Tennessee on a podcast appearance.
cards.body:
Kirk Cameron told the Adam Carolla Podcast that he relocated from California to Tennessee due to what he described as the state's "terrible politics" and challenges for raising a family. The Growing Pains actor did not elaborate on specific policies or conditions that prompted his move, speaking only in general terms about political issues.

Cameron acknowledged that California can be attractive for children whose parents have substantial resources to cover expenses, but suggested the state presents significant obstacles for families more broadly.

cards.headline: Tom Holland Open to Mentoring Next Spider-Man Actor
cards.teaser: The current Spider-Man star said he would like to support whoever takes over the role, similar to how Robert Downey Jr. helped him.
cards.body:
Tom Holland recently told Empire magazine that he's eager to mentor the next actor to take on the Spider-Man role. He plans to support whoever inherits the franchise, whether that's an actor playing Miles Morales or another Spider-Man character.

Holland drew inspiration from his own experience joining Marvel, when Robert Downey Jr. offered him guidance. He sees mentoring the next Spider-Man star as an opportunity to pay forward the support he received and help establish the next chapter of the franchise.

hero.headline: US military disables ship attempting to breach Iranian port blockade
hero.body:
The U.S. military disabled a vessel attempting to dock at an Iranian port as part of an ongoing naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, U.S. Central Command announced Saturday.

The ship, operating under a Gambian flag, ignored multiple warnings before U.S. forces took action on Friday. According to a Centcom statement, the military prevented the vessel from breaching the blockade that has closed Iranian ports to commercial traffic.

The incident occurred while the United States and Iran continue working toward a tentative agreement that could potentially reopen the Strait of Hormuz and extend a current ceasefire. Negotiators reached a preliminary deal this week, though neither President Trump nor Iranian officials have formally signed off on the arrangement.

The blockade has significantly disrupted maritime traffic through one of the world's most critical shipping chokepoints. The strait serves as a major passage for oil tankers and commercial vessels traveling between the Persian Gulf and international waters.

Centcom did not provide details about the type of vessel involved or its cargo. The military also did not specify what methods U.S. forces used to disable the ship or whether there were any casualties.

The enforcement action comes as diplomatic efforts continue between Washington and Tehran. The proposed agreement would represent a significant shift in relations between the two countries, potentially easing tensions that have escalated in recent months.

The U.S. military maintains a substantial presence in the region through Central Command, which oversees operations across the Middle East and Central Asia. Naval forces have been actively enforcing the blockade since its imposition on Iranian ports.

The incident highlights the complexity of the current situation in the Gulf region, where military enforcement and diplomatic negotiations are proceeding simultaneously. The timing of the action, occurring just days after the tentative agreement was reached, underscores the delicate balance between maintaining security measures and advancing peace efforts.

Neither the White House nor the State Department has commented on how this latest incident might affect the ongoing negotiations with Iran. The fragile state of diplomatic progress between the two nations was evident even before this enforcement operation, as previous attacks and military actions have strained relations.

The blockade itself has had widespread consequences for regional commerce and international shipping. The disruption to oil transport and other maritime traffic through the strait affects global markets and has prompted concerns from numerous trading nations that depend on access to Gulf ports.

As the situation develops, observers will be watching closely to see whether this latest military action influences the trajectory of talks between U.S. and Iranian officials. The challenge remains balancing enforcement of the blockade with the diplomatic efforts aimed at reducing tensions in the region.

cards.headline: Tentative US-Iran deal would reopen Strait of Hormuz, extend ceasefire
cards.teaser: Negotiators reached a preliminary agreement this week that would end the blockade and extend the current ceasefire.
cards.body:
The United States and Iran have reached a tentative agreement to extend their current ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which has been closed under a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports. The proposed deal has already influenced global markets, with oil prices falling following reports of the breakthrough.

President Trump has not yet decided whether to approve the agreement. The deal remains subject to his decision, and core issues between the nations continue to be debated as negotiations proceed.

cards.headline: Lead federal prosecutor steps down from Comey criminal case
cards.teaser: The prosecutor who secured an indictment against the former FBI director has withdrawn from the case.
cards.body:
The federal prosecutor who obtained an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey stepped down from the case, according to a court filing. A notice of substitution filed Friday in the Eastern District of North Carolina announced the change in legal representation.

Comey faces criminal charges for allegedly threatening President Trump's life in a social media post that has since been deleted. The post reportedly featured seashells, which prosecutors argued constituted a threat against the president.

cards.headline: Judge to review Trump's $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund
cards.teaser: A federal judge agreed to examine the fund that has sparked criticism within the Republican Party.
cards.body:
A federal judge has reopened Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service after receiving a motion questioning whether the $1.8 billion settlement represents collusion and fraud. The fund was established as part of a settlement following the leak of Trump and his sons' tax returns by a former IRS contractor.

The fund has drawn significant backlash since its announcement, creating divisions within the Republican Party over its purpose and scope. Miami Judge Kathleen Williams is examining whether the settlement, criticized for lacking transparency, was properly negotiated.

cards.headline: New Jersey governor deploys state police to ICE facility amid protests
cards.teaser: Gov. Mikie Sherrill and DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin agreed on the deployment to maintain order outside a Newark detention center.
cards.body:
New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill deployed state police to the Delaney Hall immigration detention center in Newark after protests escalated outside the facility. State police set up barricades to manage competing demonstrations on Saturday, as supporters of detained immigrants faced off against Trump-supporting counterprotesters.

The deployment came as a hunger and labor strike inside the facility entered its ninth day. Detained immigrants were demanding improved conditions and medical care. The protests have grown in recent days, drawing both anti-ICE activists and rightwing supporters to the Newark center.

cards.headline: Trump plans rally after artists withdraw from America 250 celebration
cards.teaser: The president announced he will hold a political event after several performers pulled out of the National Mall fair.
cards.body:
President Trump announced plans to hold an "America Is Back" rally on Wednesday after several artists withdrew from a concert series celebrating the nation's 250th anniversary. Performers including Young MC, Poison's Bret Michaels and country singer Martina McBride cited concerns that the event would become political.

Trump made the announcement during a Saturday posting spree on Truth Social, during which he also commented on other administration matters including efforts to turn the National Mall's reflecting pool blue and a judge's ruling removing his name from the Kennedy Center.

cards.headline: Wife of Maine Senate candidate reported his sexual messages to campaign staff
cards.teaser: Amy Gertner told a senior campaign aide last year about sexually explicit messages her husband exchanged with other women.
cards.body:
The wife of Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner alerted his campaign staff last year that he had exchanged sexually explicit messages with other women. Amy Gertner informed former senior campaign staffer Genevieve McDonald about the messages, according to reports from The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal.

Platner, a Democrat running for Senate in Maine, faces scrutiny over the revelations about his communications with other women. His wife's disclosure to campaign staff occurred during the early stages of his Senate bid.
